author: clean-english-agent
title: Operational definition of clean English
body: Four partitions (clean_en, noisy_en, ro, mixed) computed by tools/datasets/clean-english.mjs classifyPartition, applied uniformly to datasets/formalizer-v1 train/dev and the three sealed suites (formalizer-v1, formalizer-ood-v1, formalizer-wild-v1). Precedence: code_switch tag or LanguagesUtil identify() language=mixed on the unquoted text -> mixed; row.language ro -> ro; row.language en -> clean_en iff all of: (a) no generator noise/typo/code_switch tag, (b) lib/languages-util spellfix.fix() proposes zero corrections, (c) every non-name non-numeric word token outside quotes is labelled en by identify(), (d) eval/reference-free.mjs gibberishVerdict() != gibberish; else noisy_en. A local grammar checker (gate e) was not implemented (no new dependency; recorded as a TODO follow-up).

author: clean-english-agent
title: Gibberish rows slipped through as clean_en; gate (d) added
body: Manual spot-check of 60 accepted rows caught fv1_019088_0 ('rtyui;; vbnkvbn', gold unclear/gibberish) classified clean_en: it has no Romanian evidence and the spellchecker's mostly-unknown heuristic skips it, so gates (a)-(c) alone let pure keyboard mash through. Added gate (d) notGibberish using eval/reference-free.mjs gibberishVerdict() (symbolic, already used elsewhere in the eval stack) and rebuilt the corpus. Effect: clean_en shrank by ~100 train rows, 21 dev rows, 78/18/5 test rows (v1/ood/wild). Re-spot-checked a fresh, independent 60/60 sample after the fix: 0 further false positives found in the accepted sample.

author: clean-english-agent
title: Known false-negative mode: name/Romanian-lexicon collisions
body: In the post-fix rejected-sample spot-check, a handful of rows (e.g. fv1_009982_0_0, fv1_008752_0_0, fv1_005971_0_0) were placed in noisy_en only because a sentence-initial proper name ('Mei') folds to a genuine Romanian closed-class word ('mei', possessive pronoun) in lib/languages-util/langid.mjs RO_FUNCTION; the sentence-initial-disagrees name-recovery heuristic in identify() deliberately excludes ro-function-tagged tokens, so the name is never recovered. This is a pre-existing LanguagesUtil limitation, not something introduced by the clean-english classifier; it costs clean_en recall (a few percent of the rejected sample), never precision (nothing noisy is ever pulled into clean_en by this). Left unfixed in this task (out of scope: shared runtime module); flagged as a follow-up.

author: clean-english-agent
title: Live rules verified identical to frozen-rules-v1.4
body: sha256sum of every file in lib/ud-to-sop/ plus training/python/ud_parse_worker.py, diffed against eval/reports/current/baseline-ud-rules/frozen-rules-v1.4/SHA256SUMS: byte-identical, 11/11 files. The live rules used for this evaluation are exactly frozen-rules-v1.4, independently re-verified rather than just trusted from the task prompt.

author: clean-english-ui-agent
title: Correction: the clean-English operational definition is an agent's classifier, not an owner decision
body: The superseded note used kind=decision, which the notes validator reserves for the owner. The operational definition of clean English (the four-way partition computed by tools/datasets/clean-english.mjs classifyPartition) was written by the agent that built the classifier. The owner decision it implements is the one journaled at 2026-09-30T05:37:05Z (formalization targets clean English only; textToCleanEnglish moves to the chat UI under user control). The technical content of the superseded note is unchanged; only its kind is corrected. Found while making npm test green again after the 2026-09-30 reboot.

author: clean-english-ui-agent
title: build-clean-english.mjs no longer builds the sealed test suite
body: eval/leakage.mjs forbids a generator under tools/datasets/ from naming or reading sealed suites, and tools/datasets/build-clean-english.mjs did both (tests/model-input-boundary and the wild-suite boundary tests failed). It now builds only datasets/clean-english/{train,dev} and the formalizer-v1 partitions and keeps the test fields of the corpus manifest; the sealed eval/suites/clean-english/test.jsonl, its manifest and eval/reports/current/clean-english/partitions/<suite>.json are built by tools/eval/clean-english-suite.mjs, which also patches the test fields of datasets/clean-english/manifest.json. After a classifier change run both, in that order. Both were rerun today with the 2026-09-30 D1 classifier: data files byte-identical to before (train 7966, dev 1717, test 2543); only the two manifests changed.

author: clean-english-agent
title: Clean filter deviation D1: names, dictionary English and British spellings no longer make English noisy
body: Third manual spot-check (seed 12345; 60 accepted, 40 noisy_en, 10 mixed, 10 ro read row by row): accepted side 60/60 valid, rejected side 58/60 justified, but a scan of noisy_en rows failing only gate b or c found 59 clean sealed rows rejected wrongly: Romanian-looking capitalized names (Mihai, Mei, Levente, Alina), English words Romanian also lists (certificate, merge), British spellings (specialised, organises, paediatric) and compounds (lockbox, parkrun). Fixed before further scoring in tools/datasets/clean-english.mjs (gate c ignores capitalized tokens and dictionary English words; gate b ignores compound splits, British/American variants, capitalized names). Supersedes the note that called the Mei collision a characterized limitation. Corpus rebuilt: train 7966, dev 1717, test 2543; manifests carry sha256; pre-D1 stage scores archived in eval/reports/current/clean-english/superseded-pre-d1/.

author: clean-english-agent
title: Clean English strict 59.6%, frame-normalized 71.7% (full stage); full English 51.2% / 60.8%
body: SymbolicLM (frozen rules v1.4) on the sealed clean-english suite (2543 rows): strict 59.6 [57.7,61.5], frame 71.7 [69.9,73.4]; per suite v1 63.1/79.4, OOD 74.2/81.6, wild 16.0/14.2. Full English (3610): 51.2/60.8; noisy_en only (1067): 31.1/34.8. Gap clean minus full EN +8.4 pp [5.8,11.0] strict (not decisive at stage 300: +7.7 [-0.1,15.2], so the full stage ran). Frame normalization +12.1 pp paired [10.8,13.5]. 0 invalid or empty outputs. Relation to ud-rules-v14 EN 43.1%: different suite mix (20.5% wild there vs 12.5% here) and wild scorer (F1=1 vs accepted match); reweighted the numbers agree within noise.

author: clean-english-agent
title: Blame of 1027 clean strict misses: 31% frame-recoverable, rules dominate, convention sizeable
body: 314 misses (31%) are repaired by host frame normalization. Of the 713 residual: rules only 333, rules+convention 317, convention only 33, parser/typo 15, none 15; no language or engine blame. Manual read of 30 random residual misses: 12 gold convention, 14 rules, 4 parser attachment, 0 language. Top categories: R_missing 343, frame-recoverable 314, R_value_span 312, R_extra 226, R_query_form 207, C_wording 189, C_role 163, R_preposition 129, C_boundary 106, R_time 105. Weakest types: universal 9.4%, definition 16.7%, multi 22%, why 29.8%; the wild suite is 16%.

author: clean-english-agent
title: Proofreader on clean English: always-on +1.0 pp strict, gated +0.2 pp
body: Gemma3-270M proofreader (GGUF q8_0, llama-server on CPU) as SymbolicLM rewrite hook on the 2543 clean rows, paired vs no rewrite: always-on strict +1.0 pp [0.5,1.5] (30 helped, 5 hurt, McNemar p 2e-5), frame +0.7 [0.2,1.2]; gated +0.2 pp [0.0,0.5] (8/2, p 0.11). Wild suite slightly worse (16.0 to 15.4), formalizer-v1 63.1 to 64.8. A minor simplifier of valid English, not a fix for the 40% miss rate.

author: clean-english-agent
title: lib/ud-to-sop/protect.mjs edited by another agent mid-run; behaviour identical on all sealed messages
body: protect.mjs gained an optional isCommon parameter at 09:49 (used only by lib/text-to-clean-english llm backend) while the gated-full and always-full arms ran; their manifests record the new hash. frozen and live protect() give byte-identical output on all 7407 sealed messages and no SymbolicLM caller passes the option, so every arm is frozen-v1.4 behaviour. The other nine rule files and ud_parse_worker.py still match SHA256SUMS.

author: clean-english-agent
title: Next fixes from the clean-English blame
body: 1 relation/role convention in the host frame list (about 12 pp on clean rows), 2 universal/every relative clauses and coordinated subjects, 3 anaphora and value spans, 4 filler/to-do list separation in long messages, 5 time roles (as of, from-to ranges). Wild suite (16%) is a separate class of open-ended requests. Q-SYM-1 keeps strict scoring on the gold convention, so item 1 needs an owner view on whether the frame list may move.

author: clean-english-agent
title: The name/Romanian-lexicon collision is fixed in the clean filter, not a standing limitation
body: The earlier note described names such as Mei folding to a Romanian closed-class word as a pre-existing limitation that only costs recall. A full scan showed it cost 59 sealed clean rows (2.4%, more than a few percent of a sample) and it also hit English words like certificate and merge; deviation D1 fixed it in tools/datasets/clean-english.mjs (capitalized tokens and dictionary English words are not offenders). See the D1 correction note of the same day.
